newsitem.title: BENIN: Benin parliament legalises voodoo holiday.
newsitem.headline: Benin parliament legalises voodoo holiday.

text.p: Parliament in Benin has adopted a law formally enshrining January 10 as a voodoo national holdiday in the West African state considered the cradle of the religion.

Authorities declared voodoo holidays on the same date in 1995 and 1996. But President Mathieu Kerekou, a born-again Christian, who took power later in 1996, decided to seek the approval of parliament.
Lawmakers passed the bill on Monday, deputies said.

About 65 percent of Benin's five million people are animists, and the country boasts more than 200 voodoo monasteries. Pope John Paul met voodoo chief priest Dagbo Hounon during a 1992 visit to Benin.
